ui_bugs.issue: Recharts still logs 4x 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' warnings on first render despite inline style width:100%/height:256 wrappers. ResponsiveContainer measures 0 on first tick likely because the outer grid parent (.grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-3) has not yet laid out when Recharts internally measures. minWidth/minHeight props on ResponsiveContainer do not suppress the warning; it fires before the observer resolves.
ui_bugs.priority: LOW (cosmetic console noise; charts render fine)

action_items: The 'inline style' fix did NOT eliminate Recharts warnings. Options: (a) render ResponsiveContainer only after container ref has a non-zero clientWidth (use useLayoutEffect + state gate); (b) drop ResponsiveContainer and pass explicit numeric width via a ResizeObserver hook; (c) accept warnings as cosmetic (they don't break rendering).
critical_code_review_comments: The warning is fired synchronously by Recharts inside ResponsiveContainer before its internal ResizeObserver reports a size. Setting parent style width/height does not help because Recharts reads its own container ref on mount. A proper fix is to conditionally render the chart after measuring the wrapper, e.g. const [w,setW]=useState(0); useLayoutEffect via ref -> setW(ref.current.clientWidth); {w>0 && <ResponsiveContainer ...>}

Recharts warnings still fire 4 times.
rca of the issue: Recharts ResponsiveContainer measures its container synchronously on first render. Even with parent div using inline style width:100%/height:256, the container's own ref reports width=-1/height=-1 before the internal ResizeObserver fires. The minWidth/minHeight props on ResponsiveContainer only affect the fallback rendered size, not suppression of the warning. Mitigation: gate chart mount on a measured non-zero width via useLayoutEffect + ref.
